actual_quote: 4.1 The Specht filtration. Order the semistandard $S$ by a linear extension of shape dominance. The Murphy cell law of [F1] preserves the corresponding higher-shape filtration, and for fixed $S$ the action on the vectors $m_{(S,t)}$ modulo higher terms is the ordinary Specht action, its coefficients being independent of the left refinement. Hence the successive quotients of the filtration are the ordinary Specht modules $S^\lambda$, each occurring once for every semistandard tableau $S$ of shape $\lambda$ and type $\rho$, which gives the multiplicity $\#\operatorname{SStd}_\rho(\lambda)$; the finite Garnir algorithm terminates in lexicographic shape/tableau order before the dominance refinement. [F1, F3, step 3.1, algebra]

authenticated_prior_clause.statement: For every commutative ring R, invertible z, ordinary finite type-A Hecke algebra H_n and composition ρ of n, xρH_n has R-basis m_(S,t)=Σ_(s:ρ(s)=S)m_st for semistandard partition-shape S of typeρ and standard t of the same shape. It has a Specht filtration with multiplicity #SStdρ(λ) of the ordinary Specht Sλ. The row-double-coset membership uses each coset word once and no quantum-factorial division. Over the generic field this number equals the trivial-character multiplicity of the ρ-row parabolic in Sλ. The explicit ordinary Garnir row-coset identity, additive nonstandard-tableau factorization, and same-column generator refinement T_a m_st≡−m_st+Σ_(u⊲s)c_u m_ut modulo higher shapes hold; row-standard straightening has no smaller-shape terms and its same-shape terms increase tableau-prefix dominance. Shape support uses the already proved ordinary Murphy dominance ideals; the finite Garnir algorithm terminates in lexicographic shape/tableau order before that dominance refinement.
authenticated_prior_clause.strategy_final_filtration_clause: Finally, order semistandard S's in a linear extension of shape dominance. The Murphy cell law preserves the corresponding higher-shape filtration. For a fixed S the action on the vectors m_(S,t) modulo higher terms is the ordinary Specht action, since its coefficients do not depend on the left refinement. Thus the successive quotients are the stated Specht modules. Over the generic field, finite-Hecke semisimplicity makes their multiplicities equal to the trivial-character multiplicities under the ρ-row parabolic by induction/restriction adjunction. This is exactly the ordinary number consumed in the higher-level Mackey count.
